core_obligations: Analyse the fibre: if it has no isolated closed point the second alternative is immediate, and otherwise split off the isolated points and pass to a neighbourhood where they become finite over the base (proof lines 40602-40620).

Assemble the product decomposition with the finite factors at the isolated points and the complementary factor carrying the non-quasi-finite part, and verify the listed properties (proof lines 40620-40634).
proof_roadmap: Split the isolated points of the fibre (proof lines 40602-40620).
Build the product decomposition and check its properties (proof lines 40620-40635).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a finite type map and a prime of the base there is an etale neighbourhood over which the base change splits as a product of finite factors, each with a unique prime over the point, and a remainder that is quasi-finite nowhere over that point (statement lines 40578-40600). The proof does not work under a quasi-finiteness assumption: it analyses the fibre, splits off its finitely many isolated closed points, spreads them out to finite factors over an etale neighbourhood, and verifies the listed properties for the resulting decomposition (proof lines 40602-40635). Separating the isolated points of the fibre is the step that produces the finite factors. H2.
